The team's calibration kernel using this exact pattern was verified at 1.00x on every shape by the same checker and is excluded from agent success counts.
change: keep the partition dimension at 128 and stack k-chunks along the free (second) dimension; slice operands from the resident cache
measured: calibration kernel: 589,824 / 2,359,296 / 1,572,864 / 3,670,016 bytes = exactly the byte floor on all four shapes
kernel:
# WRONG (what the checker rejects): one cache shaped [K, M]
#   -> 'dma_copy dst partition dimension 256 exceeds maximum 128' when K > 128
# RIGHT: the partition dimension stays 128; k-chunks live along the free dimension
cache = nl.ndarray((128, k_tiles * M), dtype=lhsT.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
for kk in nl.affine_range(k_tiles):
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=cache[:, kk * M:(kk + 1) * M],
                  src=lhsT[kk * 128:(kk + 1) * 128, :])
# operand views for output tile m0 / n0 and k chunk kk (same rules for the rhs cache):
lhs_tile = cache[:, kk * M + m0 * 128 : kk * M + (m0 + 1) * 128]
rhs_tile = rhs_cache[:, kk * N + n0 * 512 : kk * N + (n0 + 1) * 512]
